title: Transcriptome combined with Mendelian randomization to identify key genes related to polyamine metabolism in childhood obesity and elucidate their molecular regulatory mechanisms.
authors: Sun, Manman; Zhang, Pei; Yang, Sheng; Qiao, Yunyang; Shen, Xuepo; Ji, Jialing; Ding, Ling
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和孟德尔随机化识别儿童肥胖中多胺代谢关键基因，并构建TF-mRNA网络，但核心是基因表达与临床关联，缺乏蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘涉及转录因子调控。
abstract: Currently, research has found a close correlation between childhood obesity (CO) and elevated levels of polyamines in the bloodstream. Thus, the identification of key genes associated with polyamines metabolism in CO could offer fresh insights for clinical management of CO. This study utilized two datasets from public databases (GSE205668 and GSE104815) and 59 polyamines metabolism-related genes (PMRGs) to screen for candidate genes. Subsequently, candidate key genes were selected using Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis, and machine learning algorithms were employed to obtain intersecting feature genes based on the MR results. Then key genes were identified through expression validation. Finally, we conducted research on the key genes including gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration, and transcription factor(TF)-mRNA network. Differential analysis identified 432 candidate genes linked to childhood obesity and polyamine metabolism, with 4 key genes showing causal relationships. Specifically, WWC1, NPL, and LAPTM5 as risk factors [odd ratio (OR) > 1], while GPAT3 (OR < 1) was identified as a protective factor for CO. Machine learning algorithms pinpointed 3 feature genes (WWC1, NPL, and GPAT3) with significant differential expression and consistent trends. GSEA revealed ribosome and lysosome pathways linked to key genes. MITF regulated these genes in the TF-mRNA network. Twelve immune cell types, mostly correlating with key genes, were identified. We identified 3 key genes (WWC1, NPL, and GPAT3) related to polyamine metabolism in CO. Additionally, we investigated their potential biological functions and regulatory mechanisms, aiming to provide new theoretical basis for the treatment and diagnosis of CO.
abstract_zh: 目前，研究发现儿童肥胖（CO）与血液中多胺水平升高之间存在密切相关性。因此，识别与CO中多胺代谢相关的关键基因，可为CO的临床管理提供新的见解。本研究利用来自公共数据库的两个数据集（GSE205668和GSE104815）及59个多胺代谢相关基因（PMRGs）来筛选候选基因。随后，通过孟德尔随机化（MR）分析选择候选关键基因，并基于MR结果采用机器学习算法获取交集特征基因。然后通过表达验证确定关键基因。最后，我们对关键基因进行了基因集富集分析（GSEA）、免疫浸润及转录因子（TF）-mRNA网络研究。差异分析识别出432个与儿童肥胖和多胺代谢相关的候选基因，其中4个关键基因显示出因果关系。具体而言，WWC1、NPL和LAPTM5为风险因素[比值比（OR）> 1]，而GPAT3（OR < 1）被确定为CO的保护因素。机器学习算法确定了3个特征基因（WWC1、NPL和GPAT3），这些基因具有显著差异表达且趋势一致。GSEA揭示了与关键基因相关的核糖体和溶酶体通路。在TF-mRNA网络中，MITF调控这些基因。识别出12种免疫细胞类型，其中大多数与关键基因相关。我们确定了CO中与多胺代谢相关的3个关键基因（WWC1、NPL和GPAT3）。此外，我们研究了它们的潜在生物学功能和调控机制，旨在为CO的治疗和诊断提供新的理论基础。
